text:
Riley: Quick Friday micro-debate: is it okay to claim the office shamrock plant as "our mascot" after you accidentally watered it with hot sauce? :shamrock:
Tara: Hot sauce watering is a crime against botany. Mascot status still pending. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
Jude: Depends on whether the shamrock now likes spicy food. If yes, it's resilient and earns mascot stripes.
Olivia: One-liner: "If the plant starts asking for salsa, it's officially a coworker." :joy:
OpsBot: FYI: Kitchen plants are part of communal property. Please don't add condiments to the watering schedule. :no_entry_sign:
SnackBot: New poll by Riley: "Shamrock mascot status" 1: Immediate coronation, 2: Hold a fundraiser (chips), 3: Rehab first. Poll ends in 24h.
Nate: I vote 2. Fundraiser in chips sounds like science funding.
Tara: Also, if you're going to test capsaicin tolerance, disclose it to the plant first. Consent matters.
Jude: Note: watering schedule now includes 'emotional support compliments' on Mondays. I'll draft a sticky.
Olivia: Tiny bet: whoever remembers to bring plant-friendly fertilizer gets a $2 coffee. Low-stakes incentive.
Riley: Suggestion: label with "Riley's shamrock (spicy?)" so future generations know what happened.
OpsBot: Reminder: please label any experimental plants and log unusual additives in #general. Hazmat for salsa-adjacent experiments.
SnackBot: Poll created: "Shamrock mascot status" 1: Coronation, 2: Chips fundraiser, 3: Rehab. Current votes: 1:2, 2:1, 3:1.
Tara: Final quip: "If it survives, it's earned the nickname 'Little Hotleaf.'" :leafy_green:
Jude: I'll Photoshop a tiny crown later. Low-effort, high morale.
Olivia: Closing wisdom: water plants with water, snacks with dignity. :coffee:
Riley: Thanks team. Mascot committee adjourned until snack proceeds arrive. :tada:
